mainTopic: Why the תורה needs both 'לאביו' and 'לאמו' in the פרשה of נזיר according to רבי עקיבא, and the start of a new question about the פסוק of כהן גדול.
overview: This amud continues the discussion of how רבי עקיבא reads the פסוקים about a נזיר and a כהן גדול. According to רבי עקיבא, the rule that a כהן גדול (with or without נזירות) must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה comes from the word 'לאחיו'. So the גמרא asks why the פסוק also needs to say 'לאביו ולאמו'. The answer is צריכי: both words are needed. If only 'אביו' were written, we might think the ban rests on fatherhood being only a חזקה, and allow becoming טמא for a mother, whom we know gave birth to him. If only 'אמו' were written, we might allow becoming טמא for a father, since family lineage follows the father ('לבית אבותם'). So the תורה writes both, and he may not become טמא for either parent. The גמרא then asks a new question: according to רבי עקיבא, why is 'ועל כל נפשות מת לא יבא', said about the כהן גדול, needed? The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא need 'for his father and for his mother'?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, the rule about a מת מצוה comes from 'לאחיו', whether he is just a כהן גדול or a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר. So the words 'לאביו ולאמו' seem extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא: it makes no difference whether he is only a כהן גדול or a כהן גדול who is also a נזיר. Either way, the rule comes from 'for his brother'. So why do I need 'for his father and for his mother'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that, in רבי עקיבא's reading, the words 'לאביו ולאמו' in the נזיר פסוק seem unneeded. It asks why they are there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא already draws his lesson from 'לאחיו', and it works for any כהן גדול, נזיר or not. A general ban on becoming טמא for any dead body should already cover a father and mother. So the גמרא wants to know what the extra words add.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider / after all: introduces a logical setup
Why do I need it? (asks about a seemingly extra word or verse)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי לָא שְׁנָא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לְחוֹדֵיהּ
phrases.english: now consider: it is no different whether it is a High Priest alone

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְהוּא נָזִיר,
phrases.english: and it is no different whether it is a High Priest who is also a nazir;
it is derived from 'for his brother',
phrases.notes: This comes from במדבר 6:7, and the lesson is that he must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: so why do I need 'for his father and for his mother'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how רבי עקיבא reads the פסוקים of נזיר and כהן גדול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the words 'לאביו ולאמו' add, if רבי עקיבא already learns his rule from 'לאחיו'?

steps.title: Both are needed: if only 'his father' were written
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה wrote only 'father', we might think the reason is that fatherhood is only a presumption. Then we would allow becoming טמא for a mother, since motherhood is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are both needed. If the פסוק wrote only 'his father', I would have said this is the reason he may not become טמא for him: it is only a presumption that this man is his father. But his mother, whom we know gave birth to him, let him become טמא for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: both words are needed. Here it explains why 'אביו' alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can be fully sure who his father is. We only rely on a חזקה. Someone could therefore think the ban applies only to a father and not to a mother, whose birth of the child is known for sure. So 'אמו' has to be written.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an initial, mistaken assumption)
A presumption: something assumed true but not proven

phrases.english: They are necessary:
for if it had written only 'his father',
I would have said:
this is the reason he may not become impure for him:
because it is merely a presumption.
phrases.notes: Meaning, we just assume this man is his father. We can't know it for certain.

phrases.english: But his mother, whom we know gave birth to him,
let him become impure for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each word teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'אביו', the ban might rest on fatherhood being uncertain. Then a mother would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אמו' is needed to forbid the mother too.

steps.title: If only 'his mother' were written
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה wrote only 'mother', we might think the ban comes from lineage not following the mother. Then we would allow becoming טמא for a father, since lineage follows the father. So the פסוק teaches both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה wrote only 'his mother', I would have said: for his mother he may not become טמא, because a child's lineage does not follow her. But his father, since the Master taught 'by their families, by their fathers' house', I might say let him become טמא for him. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. It explains why 'אמו' alone would not be enough, so 'אביו' is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family identity (משפחה) follows the father, not the mother. So a father might seem like a closer relative, one the נזיר should be allowed to become טמא for. Writing 'אביו' blocks that idea. In the end, he may not become טמא for either parent.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: the תורה‎ / ה׳
By their fathers' house: lineage follows the father

steps.whatToRemember: Each parent has its own reason we might have allowed it. A mother is certain; a father defines lineage. So the תורה writes both 'אביו' and 'אמו' to forbid a נזיר from becoming טמא for either.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'his mother',

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אִמּוֹ לָא לִיטַמֵּא לַהּ,
phrases.english: I would have said: for his mother he may not become impure,
since her offspring does not follow her.
phrases.notes: Meaning, a person's family lineage is counted through the father, not the mother.

phrases.english: But his father, since the Master said
'by their families, by their fathers' house',
I might say: let him become impure for him.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכותא begun in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'אמו', the ban might rest on lineage not following the mother. Then a father would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words are needed. A נזיר may not become טמא for his father or his mother.

steps.title: Why is 'he shall not go in to any dead bodies' needed?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: according to רבי עקיבא, why is the כהן גדול פסוק 'ועל כל נפשות מת לא יבא' needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'and he shall not go in to any dead bodies'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the פסוק about a כהן גדול and asks what it adds according to רבי עקיבא. This is a setup line; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא checked whether every phrase in the נזיר פסוק is needed, it now checks the כהן גדול פסוק. It asks what 'ועל כל נפשות מת לא יבא' teaches that is not already known.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not come / go in

phrases.english: 'And he shall not go in to any dead bodies',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:11, said about the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: why do I need it?
